label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: A newsletter and SMS signup popup opened by itself right after I moved focus to a product link. Keyboard focus stayed on the page link behind it instead of moving into the popup, so I only found out about it from the dialog appearing in the tree.

element.name: Unlock free shipping on orders over $2,000.

findings.problem: The popup Close button was announced as being inside an embedded payment field, which is confusing and misleading on a signup popup.

After Add to cart the cart drawer opened with Remove, Quantity, Increase quantity and Checkout Now all disabled and the subtotal empty, with no loading message. I had to re-read the page to learn that it had finished loading.

The page says Ships in 6-8 weeks next to the Add to cart button, but a section lower down says Ready to ship with in-stock inventory. These contradict each other, so I could not tell whether the item was really in stock.
On arrival the checkout page was nearly empty (only a heading and empty regions) with no loading announcement. The form only appeared after I re-read the page.
